# GitHub Pull Request #74

## Title
feat: add a thinking_level input (default: pi's medium)

## Description
"Closes #66.\n\npi-action never set a thinking level, so pi-durable's `resolveAgent` used `state?.thinkingLevel ?? \"off\"`: every run was **off**, also with `model_reasoning: true`. This adds `thinking_level`, with pi's default `medium`.\n\n## Changes\n\n- **Input.** `thinking_level`: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max` (pi-ai's `ModelThinkingLevel`, which includes `max`). Any case. Empty → `medium`. An invalid value fails the run with the list of valid values. `src/index.ts` now reads the inputs inside the promise chain, so the error reaches `setFailed` instead of crashing.\n- **Every run.** `Thread.open` adds `thinkingLevel` to the agent that `configureAgent` passes to `root.configure`, so a continuing thread switches to the new level.\n- **Capping.** pi-durable sends the level as it is (`reasoning: level`). pi-action caps it first with pi-ai's `clampThinkingLevel`, as pi does: `off` for a model without reasoning (built-in metadata, or `model_reasoning: false`); `xhigh`/`max` only when the model's `thinkingLevelMap` has them, else `high`. A capped level writes a log line, for example `thinking_level: faux/faux-1 has no reasoning support; using off`.\n- **Provider mapping (checked in pi-ai 1.5.2).** anthropic-messages: no `reasoning` → thinking disabled; `compat.forceAdaptiveThinking` → effort (via `thinkingLevelMap`); else a thinking budget. openai-completions clamps again and sends `reasoning_effort` only with `supportsReasoningEffort`.\n- **Setup log.** `🤖 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · thinking medium · tools: …`\n- **Docs.** README inputs table, `action.yml`, a new [Thinking](docs/models.md#thinking) section in `docs/models.md`, and the `🤖` examples in `docs/how-it-works.md` and `docs/extensions.md`.\n\n## Tests\n\n- Parsing: default, every level in any case, rejection of invalid values.\n- Faux provider (with a reasoning model): the level reaches the request options (`options.reasoning`); `off` (no `reasoning`) and a log line for a model without reasoning; `xhigh` → `high`; no level → unchanged.\n- A stored thread that runs with `low`, then from a new clone with `high`, sends `high`.\n- `run.test.ts`: the setup lines with the downgrade line and `thinking off`.\n\n`npm run check` passes.\n\n## Release note (for the next release)\n\n```markdown\n### Changed\n- **Runs think at pi's default level, medium** (#66, added in #74). pi-action now sets a thinking level on every run, with the new `thinking_level` input (`off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`). Before, every run was `off`. Runs on models with reasoning can now use more tokens and time. To keep the old behavior, set `thinking_level: off`. Models without reasoning support get `off`, with a log line. See [Thinking](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/vX.Y.Z/docs/models.md#thinking).\n```"

## Your Reply

pi-action posts your final response as a comment on this issue or pull request. **Do not post your reply yourself**, for example with `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, or `gh api`. That would post the same answer twice. Use `gh` to comment only where the task asks for it, such as on another issue.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.

@@ -95,6 +95,25 @@ The runner sends the requests. A `localhost` or LAN address must be reachable fr
 
 For Anthropic-compatible endpoints (`provider_api: anthropic-messages`) with Claude Opus 4.6+ or Sonnet 4.6+, set `compat_force_adaptive_thinking: true`.
 
+## Thinking
+
+`thinking_level` sets how much the model thinks (reasons) before it answers. The default is `medium`, as in pi. A higher level can give better answers to difficult tasks, but it uses more tokens and more time. To turn thinking off, set `off`:
+
+```yaml
+with:
+  thinking_level: off   # or minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max
+```
+
+- **Every run.** pi-action sets the level at the start of each run. A thread that started with a different level uses the new level from the next run, as it does for `model`.
+- **Models that support less.** pi-action caps the level as pi does (pi-ai's `clampThinkingLevel`), and writes a log line, for example `thinking_level: openai/gpt-4o has no reasoning support; using off`:
+  - A model without reasoning support gets `off`. pi knows this for its built-in models. For a custom model, set `model_reasoning: true` when the model supports reasoning.
+  - `xhigh` and `max` apply only to the models that pi maps to them. Other reasoning models get `high`.
+  - For other levels that a model does not support, it gets the next level up that it supports, else the next level down.
+- **How the level gets to the model.** The provider API changes the level into its own option. For example, Anthropic models with adaptive thinking get an effort (for a custom model, set `compat_force_adaptive_thinking`), and older Anthropic models get a thinking budget. OpenAI-compatible APIs get a reasoning effort when the provider supports it (`compat_supports_reasoning_effort`).
+- **Output tokens.** Thinking counts toward the output tokens of the model (`model_max_tokens` for a custom model).
+
+The `🤖` line of the log shows the level of the run, for example `🤖 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · thinking medium · tools: read, write, edit, bash`.
+

+	let seen: SimpleStreamOptions | undefined;

+		(_context, options) => {
+			seen = options;
+			return fauxAssistantMessage("ok");
+		},
+	]);

+	await submission.wait(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
+	return seen?.reasoning;

+/**
+ * `requested`, capped as pi caps it to what the model supports (pi-ai's `clampThinkingLevel`): `off` for a model

+ */
+function supportedThinkingLevel(
+	model: Model<Api>,
+	requested: ModelThinkingLevel,
+	log: Pick<Log, "info">,
+): ModelThinkingLevel {
+	const level = clampThinkingLevel(model, requested);
+	if (level !== requested) {
+		const why = model.reasoning
+			? `does not support thinking level ${requested}`
+			: "has no reasoning support";
+		log.info(
+			`thinking_level: ${model.provider}/${model.id} ${why}; using ${level}`,
+		);
+	}
+	return level;
